summary: The census supports three strong, file-grounded conclusions: the user's ChEMBL-37 table is ~80% the same molecules and numerically near-identical to the briford ChEMBL snapshot (median Δ=0.0 on matched hts rows), it adds essentially nothing to TEST nearest-neighbour coverage (+0.0006 mean max-Tanimoto, 4/750 queries改善), and its genuinely new content is metadata rather than chemistry — 13,559 censored upper-bound records, replicate counts, and an explicit hts-vs-literature provenance split that briford's pIC50≥4.0 equality-only file discards. The weakest parts of the current framing are treating the user table as one label column (56% of rows are a single qHTS campaign, 44% literature IC50 of which half are censored) and using max-Tanimoto as the only coverage metric, which structurally understates augmentation value. I recommend shipping the workbook as a provenance-and-censoring census with per-endpoint label counts, and running four cheap verification checks that would convert the biggest inferences into facts.
recommendation: Ship the comparative workbook, but restructure the headline table around (a) labels per endpoint, (b) provenance block (single HTS campaign vs literature vs organiser assay), (c) censoring status, and (d) official-split contamination, rather than around dataset row counts. Keep every y-semantics claim as "source label, unverified". Before any future training-set decision, run four cheap, decisive checks: (1) join user `hts` rows to pubchem_all_isoforms.csv `pic50` by normalized parent+isoform — if Δ≈0 you have verified the units and aggregation for 56% of the user's rows without the user's script; (2) compare your computed 182 TRAIN-overlapping briford parents against that file's own `in_challenge_train` flag and the blog's claimed 185, which independently validates your whole normalization pipeline; (3) add neighbour-density metrics (count of reference parents at Tanimoto ≥0.4 and ≥0.5 per TEST query, plus a second fingerprint such as AtomPair) alongside max-Tanimoto, since max is monotone in pool size and saturates; (4) compute per-source fraction inside the TEST q05–q95 physicochemical envelope, which is the same admission criterion lachrymator's README describes and is therefore directly comparable without their molecule table. Explicitly list the 4 user parents matching TEST and the 29 Ours_ChEMBL_used parents matching Official_TDI/Emax as contamination items to be excluded or fold-aligned, and do not use the 4 TEST-matching rows as any kind of performance estimate.
verified_facts: Structure-level duplication is the dominant fact about the user table: 22,129 of 27,815 user parents (79.6%) are already in Briford_ChEMBL_raw (tables/pairwise_overlap.csv:8); 23,320 are in the union of existing sources and only 4,495 are novel (summary.json:10-11).

Numerical agreement on matched structure+CYP is essentially exact for the hts block: median Δ=0.0, 99.5-99.9% within 0.1, Pearson 0.998-0.9998 vs Ours_ChEMBL_used; ic50 block median |Δ|=0.002, 94-97% within 0.1 (tables/paired_activity_statistics.csv:2-17).

TEST neighbourhood gain from the user's novel chemistry is negligible: median max-Tanimoto is 0.5873 from TRAIN alone, 0.5909 from all 44,639 labelled parents, and 0.5909 after adding the 4,491 novel user parents (mean +0.00059, summary.json:16); only 4 of 750 TEST queries gain anything, largest +0.1998 for OCNT-2535303 (tables/test_coverage_increment.csv).

The user table is two structurally different blocks under one y column: 34,142 rows (56.1%) are task=hts, all relation=point; 26,740 rows are task=ic50, of which 13,559 (50.7% of the ic50 block, 22.3% of all rows) are upper_bound (tables/user_target_task_relation.csv).

Censoring metadata is internally consistent: missing_spread=13,559 exactly equals the upper_bound row count, bound_with_points=0, duplicate_gene_inchikey_task=0 (quality.json:5-11), so each molecule/gene/task has exactly one row that is either a point or a bound, never both.

any_preinc is 0.0 in every hts group and 10.5-13.4% in every ic50 group (tables/user_flags.csv:18-25), so the flag is perfectly confounded with provenance block and cannot function as a source-independent TDI proxy.

Dynamic range and floor differ sharply from the organiser data: Official_TRAIN pIC50 spans 1.91-8.02 with medians 4.27-5.13, while user point values are floored at 3.70-4.10 with medians 5.00-5.40, and Briford_ChEMBL_raw has a hard floor of exactly 4.00 (tables/activity_statistics.csv:2-17, 14-17, 34-38).
Official TRAIN is label-sparse: 6,525 label values over 4,905 rows, i.e. 1,412/1,285/1,493/2,335 labels for CYP1A2/2C9/2D6/3A4 (tables/dataset_comparison.csv:3, tables/activity_statistics.csv:14-17).
Chemical envelope differs by more than 2x in spread: TRAIN MW sd 50.5 (q05-q95 283-429) vs user MW sd 120.7 (q05-q95 230-609) (tables/chemical_statistics.csv:2,12).

Leakage filtering was applied to the used subsets but not uniformly across official tables: Ours_ChEMBL_used and Ours_Veith_used have 0 parent overlap with TRAIN and TEST where the raw versions had 182/159 and 0/1, yet Ours_ChEMBL_used still shares 29 parents with Official_TDI and Official_Emax (tables/pairwise_overlap.csv:23-26, 70, 109, 123-129).
The user table contains 4 parents (4 stereo structures) that are also Official_TEST structures (tables/pairwise_overlap.csv:4), and Briford_Veith_raw contains 1 (line 109).

Cross-isoform Spearman is low in the hts block (0.107-0.264) and moderate in the ic50 block (0.206-0.479) (tables/user_cross_target_correlations.csv), and both are computed on relation=='point' rows only (analyse.py:146,156), so censored records are excluded from every paired and correlation statistic.

Briford's live blog claims 24,918 ChEMBL skeletons, 16,546 Veith compounds and 185 structures overlapping the challenge deck (sources/briford-blog.txt:24,30); your normalization of the archived files gives 24,925 / 16,132 parents and 182 TRAIN-overlapping parents (tables/dataset_comparison.csv:8-9, tables/pairwise_overlap.csv:23).

The archived Veith file carries pic50, ac50_um, curve_class, fit_r2, hill_slope and activity_outcome, but only max_response was used, clipped to [-150,50] and averaged (source_manifest.json:92-109, analyse.py:83,88).
The archived briford ChEMBL file carries its own in_challenge_train annotation (source_manifest.json:61-89), an independent cross-check for your overlap counts that has not been used.

The lachrymator repository is write-up only: 88,683 retrieved blind-set neighbours, 4,999 admitted with calculated properties and no assay endpoints, Butina cluster-disjoint folds, and a reported finding that 100% of regression submission-endpoint pairs were worse on the blind set than in CV (median MAE +0.208) (sources/lachrymator-README.md:9-11,74-76,85,104-113).
inferences: The user's hts block is very probably PubChem AID 1851 (Veith qHTS) pAC50 ingested into ChEMBL, not an independent screen: its per-isoform quantiles are near-identical to Earlier_Jeremy_PubChem pAC50 (CYP1A2 4.1/4.5/4.8/5.2/5.7/6.5 vs 4.1/4.5/4.8/5.2/5.7/6.5), 12,406 parents overlap that source, and the ChEMBL FAQ you cite documents AID 1851 ingestion. Check (1) in the recommendation settles this.

upper_bound almost certainly means 'pIC50 is an upper bound' from a '>' concentration relation: the values are discrete at round concentrations (q25 4.3979 = 40 uM, median 4.699 = 20 uM, q75 5.0 = 10 uM) and their means (4.67-4.71) sit a half to a full log below the point means (5.29-5.55), which is the expected signature of censored inactives rather than measured potencies.

The user file is most consistent with a ChEMBL-37 extraction that retains non-equality relations and aggregates per (gene, structure, task) with spread/n_point/n_bound/n_assay provenance counters — i.e. a superset of the pChEMBL-style equality-only view that briford's floor-4.0 file represents. This remains a reconstruction, not a verified schema.

Max-Tanimoto is the wrong single metric for augmentation value: it is monotone in pool size and already saturated by TRAIN (0.5873 of 0.5909), so a near-zero gain is evidence that no closer analogue exists, not evidence that 25k additional compounds carry no training signal. Neighbour density and envelope-membership discriminate where max cannot.

The low hts cross-isoform correlations are attenuated by range restriction: the hts block has sd 0.52-0.72 and a floor at ~4.1, so 0.107-0.264 understates true cross-isoform concordance. The dense 5-isoform Veith matrix (sd 32-60, all isoforms measured per compound) is the better substrate for that biological question and is already archived.

External ChEMBL data being shifted toward potency (medians ~5.1-5.2 vs TRAIN CYP3A4 4.27) is not unambiguously harmful if lachrymator's claim that the organisers built TEST by expanding the most potent TRAIN hits is correct; the direction of that bias relative to the scored distribution is currently unknown and unknowable without TEST labels.

opportunities.item: Verify the user's y units and aggregation for 56% of rows by joining user hts rows to pubchem_all_isoforms.csv `pic50` on normalized parent+isoform. A near-zero delta converts 'units unverified' into a documented fact for the largest block of the table, without any input from the user.
opportunities.basis: source_manifest.json:92-109 shows a pic50 column is archived; tables/activity_statistics.csv:2-13 vs :70-74 shows quantile-level identity with the PubChem pAC50 subset.

opportunities.item: Cross-validate the entire normalization pipeline against briford's own in_challenge_train flag: your 182 overlapping parents vs the blog's claimed 185 vs the file's flag count. This is the only available independent audit of your FragmentParent/Uncharger key choices, and it costs one groupby.
opportunities.basis: source_manifest.json:61-89 (in_challenge_train column), sources/briford-blog.txt:25 (185 claim), tables/pairwise_overlap.csv:23 (182 computed).

opportunities.item: Add augmentation-relevant coverage metrics: per-TEST-query counts of reference parents at Tanimoto >= 0.4 and >= 0.5, and a second fingerprint (AtomPair, matching lachrymator's choice). This replaces a saturated max statistic with one that can actually rank candidate training pools.
opportunities.basis: tables/test_similarity_summary.csv:6-8 shows max-Tanimoto saturated by TRAIN alone; sources/lachrymator-README.md:117 uses AtomPair fingerprints.

opportunities.item: Compute per-source fraction inside the TEST q05-q95 physicochemical envelope (MW, cLogP, TPSA, HBD/HBA, RotB). This makes the comparative table actionable for dataset selection and is the one metric that permits apples-to-apples comparison with lachrymator's admission criterion despite their molecule table being unavailable.
opportunities.basis: sources/lachrymator-README.md:108-113 describes filtering to the held-out set's physicochemical envelope; tables/chemical_statistics.csv already holds the per-source quantiles needed.

opportunities.item: Treat the 13,559 censored upper_bound records as the user table's actual contribution and quantify what they would change: the fraction of molecules per isoform for which censored data is the only data (e.g. 2,828 of 4,438 CYP1A2 ic50 molecules), and the shift in the pooled y distribution toward TRAIN's lower median when they are included as left-censored labels.
opportunities.basis: tables/user_target_task_relation.csv (point vs upper_bound row/parent counts per gene); tables/activity_statistics.csv:34-38 shows briford's file discards everything below pIC50 4.0.

opportunities.item: Add a Veith pAC50 auxiliary head with curve_class/fit_r2 quality filters and activity_outcome-derived censoring, instead of only clipped max_response. The archived file already contains a potency column dimensionally matched to the challenge endpoint, whereas max_response is an efficacy measure, and the [-150,50] clip truncates a real upper tail (raw maxima 272.5, 668.9, 1330.3).

Report labels per endpoint rather than rows per dataset as the primary size column. TRAIN has only 1,285-2,335 labels per isoform against 4,901 molecules, which is the scarcity that justifies augmentation and the number any candidate pool should be compared against.

Test the lachrymator claim that TEST was built by expanding the most potent TRAIN hits: correlate each TEST query's nearest TRAIN neighbour similarity with that neighbour's pIC50. You already have the nearest-neighbour table, so this is a join, and the answer changes how the potency shift in external data should be read.
opportunities.basis: sources/lachrymator-README.md:74-76; tables/test_nearest_neighbors.csv exists in the artifact set.

opportunities.item: Note the loss of CYP2C19 in the user table: briford's ChEMBL and Veith files cover five isoforms (11,188 and 17,107 CYP2C19 records) and the user file covers only the four scored ones, so the user table cannot replace those sources for multi-task auxiliary breadth.
Record the two TEST rows that collapse to one parent (750 rows, 748 parents) as an irreducible-error item: any 2D-only model must give them near-identical predictions.

risks.item: Presenting a single 'user y' distribution or a single novelty bar chart invites the conclusion that one coherent 60,882-row dataset exists. 56% of rows come from one qHTS campaign, 22% are censored bounds, and the two blocks differ in dynamic range (sd 0.52-0.72 vs 0.73-0.95), censoring (0% vs 51%) and pre-incubation annotation (0% vs 12%). Any downstream model trained on the pooled column inherits that confound silently.

The near-perfect paired agreement statistic is restricted to relation=='point' rows and therefore cannot be read as 'the user table agrees with briford'. It demonstrates agreement precisely on the subset where both sources carry equality data, which is also the subset where no new information exists.
risks.basis: analyse.py:146 filters relation=='point'; tables/paired_activity_statistics.csv covers only hts/ic50 point rows.

risks.item: 4 user parents and 1 briford Veith parent are Official_TEST structures. If the user table is ever folded into a training pool without the parent-level filter that Ours_*_used already applies, those become direct blind-set label leakage. They are also tempting as a 'free check' — with n=4 any such check is uninformative and creates a leakage path into model selection.
risks.basis: tables/pairwise_overlap.csv:4,109; contrast with lines 25-26,123,138-139 where the used subsets are clean.

risks.item: 29 parents are shared between Ours_ChEMBL_used and Official_TDI/Emax, so the historical filtering rule was 'exclude TRAIN and TEST parents', not 'exclude all official parents'. For auxiliary heads trained on TDI/Emax this puts the same molecule in both the external and the organiser block, which can inflate any CV estimate that assigns folds by official molecule.
risks.basis: tables/pairwise_overlap.csv:70,126 (29 parents) vs lines 25 and 123 (0 with TRAIN).

risks.item: Reporting 'adds no TEST coverage' from max-Tanimoto alone risks an over-strong negative conclusion about external data generally. The metric is saturated by TRAIN, computed on one fingerprint without chirality, and measures only the single closest neighbour.
risks.basis: tables/test_similarity_summary.csv:6-8; summary.json:19 documents the fingerprint and pool-size caveat.

risks.item: The cross-isoform Spearman panel is likely to be read as a selectivity result. It is computed on range-restricted, floor-truncated, censored-excluded medians of pooled literature and HTS data, and the caption's hedge may not survive extraction into a summary table.

The largest paired disagreements are dominated by Tox21 and Earlier_Jeremy_ChEMBL pairs with |delta| up to 4.5 log units, several on well-known compounds. These are not random noise; they indicate genuine endpoint incommensurability (pAC50 floor artefacts vs literature IC50) and should be reported as a reason to keep those sources on separate heads, not as outliers to be trimmed.
risks.basis: tables/paired_largest_disagreements.csv:2-25; tables/activity_statistics.csv:54-57 shows the Tox21 pAC50 floor at ~4.1 with median 4.45.

risks.item: Quoting briford's blog numbers next to yours without the normalization column will read as a discrepancy in the source rather than a difference in keying: 24,918 vs 24,925 is a rounding/version difference, but 16,546 vs 16,132 is a 414-compound gap that is most plausibly your parent-level deduplication of stereoisomers and salts.
risks.basis: sources/briford-blog.txt:24,30; tables/dataset_comparison.csv:8-9 (25,841 rows to 24,925 parents; 16,470 stereo structures to 16,132 parents).

risks.item: The lachrymator README's leaderboard numbers are self-reported by its author and the repository contains no training code or molecule table, so they cannot anchor any quantitative comparison. Its methodological statements (Butina folds, envelope filtering, CV-to-blind degradation) are usable as hypotheses and design precedent only.

alternatives: Reframe the deliverable from 'which dataset is best' to 'which label-generating process does each source sample', with one row per (source, assay campaign, endpoint, censoring status) instead of one row per file. Fifteen dataset views collapse into roughly six distinct measurement processes — organiser direct pIC50, organiser TDI-condition pIC50, organiser single-concentration log2FC, organiser Emax, the AID 1851 qHTS panel, and heterogeneous literature IC50 — which is the distinction that actually governs whether two sources can share a head.

Instead of (or before) expanding the molecule census, quantify what the censored records alone would change, since that is the only substantive asymmetry between the user table and briford's file. A Tobit/censored-likelihood head on the 13,559 bounds is a concrete, testable use; a plain-regression head on them is not.

If the goal is actually dataset selection rather than description, the census cannot answer it and no amount of overlap statistics will. The minimal decisive experiment is a fixed-architecture, Butina-fold ablation over candidate pools scored on TRAIN folds only, with the lachrymator-reported CV-to-blind degradation (median MAE +0.208) applied as an explicit discount on any CV improvement. Recommending that experiment is more useful than ranking pools from the census.

Consider dropping Tox21 and BindingDB-patents from the headline comparison and relegating them to an appendix: TEST median max-Tanimoto 0.31 and 0.26, MW medians 225 and 460 against TEST's 337, and a pAC50 floor artefact at ~4.1 make them poor candidates on every axis you have measured. Keeping them at equal visual weight implies a closer contest than the data shows.
missing_information: Whether the lachrymator repository is a third party's work or this project's own public write-up. This determines whether its leaderboard table is an external benchmark or a self-report, and the brief treats it as external while its content is methodologically adjacent to your own pipeline. The comparative table should state which it is.

The exact semantics of y_type=upper_bound (whether y is an upper bound on pIC50 or on potency, i.e. the sign of the censoring) and of `spread`, `n_bound` and `n_assay`. The round-concentration clustering strongly suggests right-censored IC50, but no documentation exists and the user declined to supply the preparation script.

Whether any_preinc derives from assay description text, a ChEMBL assay field, or a manual rule. Without this its 10.5-13.4% prevalence in the ic50 block cannot be compared to the organisers' is_tdi labels at all.

The fraction of Veith max_response values altered by the [-150,50] clip, and whether pic50/activity_outcome were available at the time that choice was made. Raw maxima of 272.5/668.9/1330.3 indicate the upper clip is doing real work.

Assay IDs and protocol metadata for the user's ic50 block, which is what would be needed to decide whether literature IC50 records can share a head with the organisers' direct-inhibition pIC50 rather than merely sharing a unit.

Whether the challenge rules permit using public assay values for TEST-set structures. The 4 overlapping parents make this a live question even though no submission is in scope; lachrymator's README documents using TEST-neighbour structures with no endpoints, which is a materially weaker use than labels.
what_would_change_view: If the user hts y values do not match pubchem_all_isoforms.csv `pic50` on matched parent+isoform, the 'one qHTS campaign' reading collapses and the user table would contain a second, genuinely independent potency source — which would raise its value substantially.

If neighbour-density metrics (count at Tanimoto >= 0.4/0.5 per TEST query) show external pools contributing many moderately-similar compounds where TRAIN contributes few, the 'adds nothing to TEST coverage' conclusion would need to be narrowed to 'adds no closer single analogue', and augmentation would look considerably more attractive.

If TEST nearest neighbours in TRAIN are systematically the high-pIC50 TRAIN compounds, the potency shift in external ChEMBL data becomes a feature rather than a domain-shift liability, and the pIC50>=4.0 floor in briford's file becomes much less costly.
If briford's own in_challenge_train flag disagrees materially with your 182 overlapping parents, the normalization keying needs re-examination before any count in the workbook is quoted as exact.

If the user supplies the preparation script or confirms the censoring direction, the single largest caveat on the whole analysis is removed and the 13,559 bounds become directly usable rather than merely countable.
escalation_reason: No decision reserved for the user is needed to finish a read-only descriptive workbook, and the recommended checks are local joins over already-archived files. Two items should be surfaced to the user in the report rather than acted on: the 4 user-table parents that are Official_TEST structures (a rules question about using public labels for blind-set compounds, which only becomes live if a future training or submission step is proposed), and the unresolved y_type/spread/any_preinc semantics that the user has already declined to document.
